content.user_title: Design Event Stores for Event-Sourced Systems
content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems need durable ordering, concurrency control, and replay safety. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design practical event store patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains event store architecture with stream and global ordering concepts.
Compares EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten tradeoffs.
Provides PostgreSQL schema templates for events, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.
Shows Python patterns for appending, reading, and subscribing to events.
Lists operational practices for idempotency, schema versioning, snapshots, and backpressure.
limitations: Examples are templates and need review before production use.
It does not deploy infrastructure, run migrations, or manage live databases.
It does not provide complete vendor operations guides or capacity models.
It assumes basic event sourcing and database knowledge.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Event Store
use_cases.description: Choose storage technology, stream strategy, indexes, and checkpointing rules for a new event-sourced service.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten against system constraints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Guardrails
use_cases.description: Define replay, retention, snapshot, idempotency, and backpressure practices before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Event Store Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain event store design for a team new to event sourcing. Cover streams, versions, ordering, subscriptions, and immutable events.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Storage Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten for my workload. My constraints are: [describe constraints].

prompt_templates.title: Design a PostgreSQL Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PostgreSQL event store for [domain]. Include tables, indexes, optimistic concurrency, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this event store design for production readiness: [paste design]. Focus on replay safety, scaling, retention, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need to choose between PostgreSQL and EventStoreDB for an order service.
output_examples.output: A concise tradeoff review covering operational fit, stream queries, subscriptions, consistency, team experience, and migration risk.

output_examples.input: Design the storage model for customer account events.
output_examples.output: A schema outline with event rows, per-stream versions, global positions, snapshots, metadata, and checkpoint tables.

output_examples.input: Check whether my projections can be rebuilt safely after failure.
output_examples.output: A review of idempotent handlers, checkpoint behavior, replay order, backpressure handling, and clean rebuild steps.

best_practices: Clarify throughput, retention, replay, and consistency needs before choosing a store.
Keep events immutable, small, versioned, and tied to correlation metadata.
Test concurrency, replay, idempotency, and projection rebuild paths with production-like data.
anti_patterns: Treating an event store as a mutable CRUD database.
Selecting Kafka or a database only because it is already available.
Skipping checkpoint, snapshot, and backpressure design until after launch.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design event stores for event-sourced systems, including streams, schemas, subscriptions, and operational practices.

faq.question: Can it choose an event store technology?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common options and maps them to workload, team, and operations constraints.

faq.question: Does it run migrations or deploy infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and implementation templates, but users must apply changes themselves.

faq.question: Does it cover PostgreSQL event stores?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes schema, indexing, concurrency, read, append, and subscription patterns for PostgreSQL.

faq.question: Is the generated design production ready?
faq.answer: No design should be used without review. Validate reliability, security, data retention, and performance in your environment.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
